subject: Integration: SDK quickstart + env setup — post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood-inference.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@luminaai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Integration: SDK quickstart + env setup — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Emily / Devon —

Great to meet you on the call earlier — thanks for walking us through the Lumina retrieval flow and the key latency targets. Quick recap from our side plus concrete next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary integration targets: chat + rerank pipeline, embedding-based retrieval for knowledge base, and a follow-up on structured tool-calling for actions (create-ticket, fetch-record).
- Preferred dev stack: Python backend + TypeScript frontend for the prototype.
- Auth constraints: must support API keys today; exploring OIDC for SSO within 2–3 sprints.
- Latency SLO: 150–200ms p95 for single-turn chat, bulk reranks can be higher with batching.

Deliverables we’ll provide by next Tuesday (26 May):
1) SDK quickstart bundle (Python + TS) with a minimal sample app wired to the hosted Redwood API (attached as redwood-integration-quickstart.zip).
2) Auth patterns doc mapping API-key and OIDC flows + recommended environment variables.
3) Routing & model guidance: suggested model variants for low-latency routing and a fallback plan for high-load windows.
4) Embeddings/reranker primer with a small synthetic prompt-set and expected P50/P95 performance.

Immediate asks from Lumina (please confirm):
- Can you share a sample KB document (anonymized) or a small set of example queries we can use for embedding tuning?
- Is Devon the engineering lead we should include on follow-ups for architecture decisions?

Next steps / meeting cadence
- I’ll drop the quickstart + runbook into the shared Drive (link below) and ping a private HubSpot activity (DEAL-9742).
- Proposed follow-up: 30-minute tech sync on Wed 27 May — options: 10:00am PT or 2:00pm PT. Let me know what works.

Attachments (stubs):
- redwood-integration-quickstart.zip (contains sample apps, README, env examples)
- lumina-map-reqs.pdf (your notes we captured on the call)

Shared links:
https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ExampleSharedRunbook
https://hubspot.redwood.example/deal/DEAL-9742

Thanks — we’ll keep this tight and focused so you can validate locally quickly.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood-inference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@luminaai.com>

Cc: Devon Price <devon.price@luminaai.com>
Date: Sat, 23 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration: SDK quickstart + env setup — post-call recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and exactly what we need. A couple quick clarifications before Wed: 

1) Sample KB: we can share a small anonymized export (~200 docs) — Devon, can you confirm?
2) Embeddings: are you recommending a single embedding model for both semantic search and rerank, or a two-model pattern? Our priority is accuracy first, then cost.
3) Local testing: will the quickstart include a local mock of the KV/DB so we can run the reranker end-to-end without sending production queries to Redwood during initial dev?

Also Wed 27 May — 10:00am PT works for us. I’ve tentatively booked that slot on our side.

Cc: Devon Price <devon.price@luminaai.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Sun, 24 May 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration: SDK quickstart + env setup — post-call recap & next steps

Emily — thanks for the quick confirmation. Answers inline and a few adjustments:

1) Sample KB: great — Devon, if you can drop the anonymized export to the Drive folder (or send a secure link), we’ll use it to build the embedding tuning config and a small evaluation prompt set. If you prefer, we can also accept a CSV of (id, text, metadata).

2) Embeddings pattern: for your initial pilot we recommend a single embedding model tuned for semantic recall (simpler ops). If you need tighter rerank precision later, we propose a two-stage pattern: cheap dense embeddings for candidate retrieval + a small reranker model (or prompt-based rerank) for top-10. We’ll include both patterns and cost/latency tradeoffs in the primer.

3) Local testing: yes — the quickstart includes a tiny local DB mock (sqlite + a small dataset) and a mock redis-like cache so you can exercise the end-to-end rerank locally without touching production. The README includes startup steps for Python (venv & pip) and TypeScript (node 18+, npm install).

Follow-up sync: Wed 27 May, 10:00am PT — I’ve sent a calendar invite and included a short agenda:
- 10m: integration goals + success criteria
- 10m: quickstart walkthrough (Python + TS sample)
- 10m: open Q&A (auth, routing, embeddings)

Deliverables ETA: we’ll upload the quickstart zip and starter runbook to the Drive by EOD Monday (25 May).

One more ask: please confirm the expected go/no-go decision date for the pilot so we can align rollout steps and reserved capacity sizing.

Thanks — excited to get you up and running.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood-inference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
